## Start here
STCA works with polymer structure–property data and repeat units. After installation, say **“Start S
TCA”** or describe the task you want to complete. See the natural-language examples for complete con
escribe the task you want to complete. See the natural-language examples for complete conversations:
| Task | Goal | A short request |
| **Upload data and learn rules** | Learn rules and return their screening results | “Learn high the

rmal-conductivity rules from this data.” |
| **Screen with existing rules** | Use bundled rules or y

our saved rules | “Screen this candidate table with existing rules.” |
| **Generate with existing ru
les** | Choose rules, then preview and confirm the prompt or generate directly | “Generate 20 candid
ates directly with this rule.” |
STCA is a skill used by your AI assistant in the conversation. The task instructions are built in: d
escribe what you need, attach your data when needed, and continue in natural language. The assistant
reads files, offers relevant rules and asks only for missing information. When learning rules, omit
ted percentages use Top or Bottom **10%, 20% and 30%** automatically; you can specify any percentage
strictly between 0% and 100%, such as **15% and 25%**. You do not enter rule IDs or manage Python.
Calculations use a CPU and support Python 3.10 or later; generation uses your current AI assistant.
Before learning, the assistant states the **structure column, property column, unit and direction**
it will use. Known datasets have built-in column mappings; for your own table, you can name the colu
mns directly. If several columns could represent the target, such as measured density, computed dens
ity or density at different temperatures, it asks you to choose before learning. See Prepare your da
or density at different temperatures, it asks you to choose before learning. See Prepare your data.
## Try an example
Download ADEPT `BANDGAP_DFT.csv` and upload it to the conversation. This file has **2,916 records an
d two columns**. The target is the **DFT HOMO–LUMO gap of a hydrogen-capped isolated monomer**, in e
two columns**. The target is the **DFT HOMO–LUMO gap of a hydrogen-capped isolated monomer**, in eV.
| Use | Column | Spreadsheet position |

| Repeat-unit structure | `SMILES` | A · column 1 |

and no unknowns**. On 584 independent Morgan-distance extrapolation records, the STCA rule has **pre
cision 0.7500, recall 0.7784, F1 0.7639 and Matthews correlation coefficient 0.6517**. Full-table ma
tches and independent evaluation are reported separately.

The assistant learns STCA and WRAcc from the training partition and returns both results. Continue w
ith **“Reload the Top 30% STCA rule just saved and screen the same file.”** Every row must match its
op 30% STCA rule just saved and screen the same file.”** Every row must match its previous decision.
**Generate with the selected rule:**

To adjust the prompt first, say **“Show the complete generation prompt before generating.”** After y
our edits, say **“Confirm and generate.”** The current LLM proposes candidates and STCA verifies the
ir exact structural conditions. See the complete ADEPT example and generated proposals.
## Save rules and continue
Learning returns STCA and WRAcc separately, with a recommendation for each tier. Recommendations use
training-side validation and the average of **Matthews correlation coefficient, precision and F1 sc
ore**, as defined in the author’s STCA paper. Say “Use the recommended rule” or name a method. Data
splitting and evaluation.
WRAcc automatically chooses its maximum condition count within the training data. You can also say *
*“Allow up to 10 WRAcc conditions”** or **“Do not limit the number of WRAcc conditions.”**
After learning, it returns **both methods’ results and rule availability for every tier**: the perce
ntage and its **numeric physical cutoff, ≥/≤ comparison and unit**, original SMILES, selection decis
ions, every unmet rule condition and uncomputable records. Cutoffs use the original physical scale e
ven when learning uses log10. Results always cover the original uploaded table; a separate candidate
table receives its own results.
The assistant saves available models, rules, physical cutoffs and complete bilingual generation prom
pts as files, and reports their names and locations. Continue by saying **“Use the rules you just sa
ved to screen this table”** or **“Use the saved gap rule to generate 20 repeat units.”** Download th
e rule bundle for use in a new session or on another platform; availability of local files depends o
n the current workspace.
When you ask to generate with existing rules, STCA **shows the available rule catalog first**, inclu
ding bundled rules and saved rule bundles loaded in the conversation. Choose a source, property and
percentage, then choose how to generate:
